quote: I cannot fathom paying $70/hour (~$3200 minimum contract) for someone to watch our kids while we are both off work.
cx: Father of one, twins on the way, arguing with his wife over hiring a postpartum doula.

quote: I think social media, some of it thinly veiled ads for doulas, is making her think if we are tired we are going to suffocate the baby in our sleep or run the car into a tree from exhaustion.
cx: He blames social media and doula marketing for his wife's fear of the newborn weeks with twins.

quote: the doulas we've contacted (well, she's contacted) have an obligation to imply scarcity and need a contract months ahead. Part of me wants to call them myself and pretend I need care in a week and see if they are "sold-out"
cx: Suspects doulas manufacture scarcity to lock in contracts months ahead.

quote: my wife said we'd need to account for about "thirty-two" for the doula, and I was like "oh hourly? that's not bad for a 'treat-yo-self' every few days"... and she was like no thirty-two hundred minimum, $65/hr (i rounded up lol).
cx: How he learned the doula's minimum contract price.

quote: You know... I think I am being kind of selfish here... she complained about lack of sleep but I didn't really dig into it with her other than that point.
cx: After a commenter asks whether his wife enjoyed the first baby as much as he did.

quote: say I'm 3 nights into my doula service and I'm feeling disconnected from my newborns, I can't just cancel on the contract. Similarly, if I don't get someone under contract and my wife is pissed at me because everyone's booked and we look like night of the living dead.
cx: The minimum contract makes the doula decision feel like a trap either way.

quote: since I got pregnant I’ve been wanting to make some last minute memories together as just a family of 3, however my mother and my mil have been demanding access to our family weekly and it’s becoming exhausting.
cx: 24 weeks with a 3.5-year-old, working full time; both grandmothers want weekly time.

quote: as she’s walking out the door she said “I’ll see you Friday and I’ll be here to pick you up Saturday to go to the park” she never even asked me if that was ok or if we have plans.
cx: Her own mother books the weekend for her on the way out.

quote: Am I just being hormonal? I feel like I’m being robbed of trying to make memories with my son as a family of 3 right now.
cx: Asking strangers if her wish for time alone with her son before baby two is unreasonable.

quote: my mom cried last Friday because I took my little guy to the park without her, it’s literally just the park.
cx: Grandmothers' reactions when left out of small outings.

quote: Usually when I don’t overshare with her she gets mad and my brothers will start calling me asking what I done to hurt her feelings so I’m always anxious about it I feel like I’m always trying to manage her emotions which has to stop.
cx: Why saying no to her mother costs her more than one conversation.

quote: She honestly just doesn't want to be touched and she recognizes it and apologizes and I tell her absolutely do not apologize.
cx: A husband on his wife's lack of desire for touch through the pregnancy.

quote: She is very stylish but for some reason doesnt want to buy maternity clothes so she rents the clothes I guess? I didnt know you could do that. […] Price maximum $1000 but I want it to be nice and memorable!!
cx: A close friend shopping for one large gift for a woman five months into her first pregnancy.

quote: We’re expecting twins towards the end of October (super excited), but I am terrified I will not have the energy to handle all 3 kids, I am also terrified that I’ll be too tired to do anything and have everything fall on my fiancés back.
cx: A manual-labour father of a 7-year-old, exhausted, before twins arrive.

quote: My biggest worry was (and will be) the socio economic environment currently and just me being able to provide (financially, emotionally, ...).
cx: A new father on what worried him before the baby came.

quote: You know what the worst part is, Im actually falling asleep more when Im holding him or feeding and NOT when he's sleeping 😅
cx: First days home: too wired to sleep when the baby sleeps.

quote: She called on Tuesday asking to visit Thursday and stay the night. Saying, “we'll take \[toddler\] out of daycare for the day to give you guys a break!” MAAM that is NOT A BREAK.
cx: Early second pregnancy, not yet announced; mother-in-law invites herself for an overnight.

quote: My first pregnancy was super easy and this one is so much harder. I'm exhausted, I'm nauseous, food is unappealing, I had to say goodbye to 70% of my closet already by like week 9
cx: Second pregnancy compared with the first, while potty training a toddler.

quote: Constantly making comments like “well all my kids were potty trained by 18 months!” and “\[toddler\] is always just an ANGEL with me and NEVER tantrums!” and “when my kids were young, i made them all their food from scratch!”
cx: What her mother-in-law says about her parenting during the visit.

quote: It's really sucking the joy out of this pregnancy. Like I'm not even excited to announce now.
cx: After telling her mother-in-law to stop policing her drinks.

quote: Under the options for leave it gives baby bonding, family health condition, pregnancy/maternity, and self health condition. Do i use the family health condition option, the pregnancy option, or the baby bonding option? My company offers 6 weeks paid bonding time
cx: A father four days after the birth trying to file FMLA in his employer's leave portal.

quote: i'm just very confused and HR never returns calls, only emails. and are not helpful when emailing.
cx: Same father on getting answers from HR about his leave.

quote: I literally have no idea what to expect, luckily she has a 5 year old already and knows damn near about everything when it comes to a new born but I'm freaking out still.
cx: First-time father days before the due date; his fiancée already has a child.

quote: I'm fully ready to give it my all, now knowing how to do that, that's something I have to learn, I just want to be the best partner/father possible.
cx: Same father: willing, but does not know how.

quote: That's what my mom keeps telling me, as soon as I see him something will change in me for the better.
cx: His mother's reassurance before the birth.

quote: On day two I was having trouble feeding and we asked them to get the bus into central London to pick up a pump etc- my mum came to tell me she was scared to get the bus
cx: Her parents' first-week visit to London, when she needed errands run.

quote: Mum then kept crying all week saying it ‘would cripple her’ not to see baby every day.
cx: Her mother during the first week after the birth.

quote: Week 4- MIL has now flown in from abroad. She did bring a bunch of food, which feels like actual help. But she is parked downstairs on the sofa with all her stuff out so there isn’t anywhere for my to sit.
cx: An overseas mother-in-law staying in their small London flat at four weeks.

quote: Overall I feel like I’m doing all the work to keep baby alive, plus quite literally sweeping up after everyone, trying to keep our small flat tidy. […] Really wish I’d banned visitors, I thought people would be here to offer help.
cx: One month in, looking back on a month of family visits.

quote: Ah yes the nursing is so awkward- especially in the heat wave it’s so annoying to having to find modest ways to cover myself!
cx: Feeding in front of visitors during a UK heatwave.
